Weekly rankings

Half-PPR projections if active, with realistic ranges. Tap a player for his full card.

How to read
Projection assumes the player is active (NFL availability is yes/no, so injured players show an Inactive% instead of a discount). The range bar comes from how past projections of this size actually turned out: thin line = floor to ceiling (10th to 90th percentile), thick bar = the likely middle half, tick = projection. Matchup: grade A-F ranks this week's matchups at the position; the pill is fantasy points this defense adds or removes vs an average one. TD donut: ring segments = chance of 0 / 1 / 2 / 3+ touchdowns (darker = more), center = chance of at least one. ECR is the FantasyPros expert consensus rank (faded "lw" = last week's, until Friday). A yellow edge marks a projection boosted by a teammate's absence.
Preset
Points per stat
League (sets the tiers)

Projections are stat lines, so any scoring re-scores them exactly. Blended-in expert ranks and the floor/ceiling ranges are scaled by the same ratio (an approximation). Saved on this device.

Power rankings

Opponent-adjusted points per game vs an average team. Everything adds up: Offense = Pass O + Run O, Defense = Pass D + Run D, Net = Offense + Defense + ST.

How to read
Every number is points per game against an average opponent: each unit's per-play rating times a league-average number of those plays (about 37 dropbacks, 24 runs and 11 special-teams plays), so the columns add up and a run edge is never read as equal to a pass edge. Hover any unit for its per-play rating. Pass O includes the team's current starting quarterback. Higher is better everywhere, including defense. Rank range is the 10th-90th percentile rank when ratings are resampled within their uncertainty (200 bootstrap resamples of games): a narrow range means the data has settled, a wide one means a few more games could move the team a lot. Colored badges are league ranks (green = top 8, red = bottom 8). Schedule: points per game the opponents took away (played) or would take away (left), unit by unit: the team's actual dropbacks against each opponent's pass defense and runs against its run defense, plus the offenses its defense faced. Positive = tougher than average; 1st = hardest. Re-scored every week with current ratings. Arrows show the move since last week.
